units.title: Anatomical position, planes, and positions
units.summary: Introduction to Anatomy Anatomy • The science of the structures & functions of the body Anatomical Position • Standing erect • Head, eyes, and toes directed anteriorly/ forward • Upper limb by the sides with palms facing anteriorly • Lower limb close together with feet parallel & toes directed anteriorly Body Planes ** Imaginary Planes Sagittal Plane divide body into RIGHT & LEFT Coronal Plane divide body into FRONT & BACK Transverse Plane divide body into Upper body & Lower body Source of Figure: Internet Terminology Related to Positions Anterior The front portion of the body Posterior The back / behind portion of the body Hand • Palmar Foot • Plantar Trunk • Ventral • Dorsal Terminology Related to Positions Describe the relative distances from the roots of limbs Proximal • towards an attached base of limb Distal • away from an attached base of limb • eg. Terminology Related to Positions Ipsilateral • refers to the same side of the body Bilateral • paired structures in both right & left sides Contralateral • refers to opposite sides of the body Supine • lying face upward Prone • lying face downward

units.title: Terminology related to movements
units.summary: Terminology Related to Movements Flexion • Joint bending movement takes place in a sagittal plane • decreasing in joint angle Extension • movement along sagittal plane that straighten the joint with increasing in joint angle. Lateral flexion • Movement of the trunk in the coronal plane Terminology Related to Movements Abduction • The limb moving away from midline of the body, along the coronal plane Adduction • The limb moving towards body in the coronal plane Rotation • Turning of a bone along its longitudinal axis Terminology Related to Movements Medial/ Internal rotation • Movement that results in the anterior surface of the body part facing medially Lateral/ External Rotation • Movement that results in the anterior surface of the body part facing laterally Circumduction • Joint movement that combines Flexion, Abduction, Extension and Adduction sequentially • Hip: https://youtu.be/5J8lmhectY4?si=kUkniLG6wDCvjyyP Terminology Related to Movements Pronation • Medial rotationof forearm in such manner that palm of hand faces posteriorly Supination • Lateral rotationof forearm from pronated position, with palm of hand faces anteriorly ** movement of radiusover the ulna Elbow https://youtu.be/PNWRcx6ZYKg?si=3rNVtKZ6Gwg5mxcW Opposition • Movement at saddle joint between metacarpal I and the trapezium
